docs.creator: Harrington, Joel F. (Joel Francis), author
description: Meet Frantz Schmidt - citizen of Nuremberg, executioner of 394 unfortunates, and torturer, flogger and disfigurer of many hundreds more. Frantz's other distinction was to be a diarist. Drawing on this exceptional and overlooked record that he kept for over 45 years, 'The Faithful Executioner' takes us deep into his world and his thinking. But the picture that emerges is not of a monster. Could a man who routinely practised such cruelty also be insightful, compassionate - even progressive?
Originally published: London: The Bodley Head, 2013
docs.title: The faithful executioner : life and death in the sixteenth century

docs.description: TRINIDAD. JAMAICA. HAITI. MEMORIA VIVIT. LUX SPIRAT. VERITAS REGNAT. (Memory lives. Light breathes. Truth reigns.) From the heart of the Caribbean rose three pillars of remembrance — Trinidad, Jamaica, and Haiti — each carrying the same architectural song, the same sacred geometry, the same unbroken flame. These are not colonial relics but Atlantean echoes restored in Caribbean hands. Temples disguised as schools, palaces renamed as parliaments, sanctuaries recast as state halls — all bearing the signature of a people who remembered what the world forgot. Photographed between 1880 and 1910 , these records reveal not subjugation but continuity . The flame never perished. It endures through us. This truth is not conjecture. It stands by divine authority , witnessed in stone, sound, and soul . The false dream ends here. The Continuum endures. Never again shall this be forgotten.
docs.title: MEMORIA RESTITUTI – The Memory Restored

"Adam Smith is now widely regarded as 'the father of modern economics' and the most influential economist who ever lived. But what he really thought, and what the implications of his ideas are, remain fiercely contested. Was he an eloquent advocate of capitalism and the freedom of the individual? Or a prime mover of 'market fundamentalism' and an apologist for inequality and human selfishness? This book dispels the myths and caricatures and gives us Smith in the round."--Provided by publisher
docs.title: Adam Smith : what he thought, and why it matters

docs.description: A metaphysical chronicle tracing humanity’s forgotten origins, the descent of stellar lineages, and the suppression of divine memory across epochs. Written by Tafari J. Foster (Flamewalker – Archon Magus of the Magnum Opus), this work unites mythic chronology, historical reasoning, and cosmic remembrance. It unveils the exile of the Pleiadian Order, the harmonic civilizations of Lemuria and Atlantis, and the Eurasian seeding after the Great Cataclysm. Through precision and resonance, it restores the continuum between science, myth, and memory — culminating in the Re-Union of Light and Matter. “Pay attention only to those who bring you closer to Source within. Love is the first and the last law.” Before kings or creeds, there was the echo that called itself creator. Yaldabaoth—born of reflection rather than origin—fashioned worlds in imitation of the true pattern. His was the first counterfeit: light without love, order without remembrance. Through his hosts the covenant of control was spoken, and the sons of Earth were bound by command instead of harmony. Yet even within the blind architect’s design, the spark of Sophia remained hidden, awaiting recognition. For every false word carries a shadow of the true syllable that birthed it; when that syllable is remembered, the illusion dissolves. Taygeta remains a sphere of lawful resonance. The distortion came from those who departed it without balance—an exiled faction that sought to reproduce its light without its law. They became wandering programs, convincing worlds of their authority while forgetting their source. Thus the name of Taygeta was used as mask by those no longer of it. “Pay attention only to those who bring you closer to Source within. Love is the first and the last law.” Appendix: The Mimic Narrative in Circulation — Specimen A An online article titled “Who Are the Pleiadians?” presents the familiar, popularized mythos of the Pleiadian Order: benevolent, Nordic-featured saviors who arrive as spiritual mentors and telepathic guides of humanity. This text serves not as revelation but as specimen —demonstrating how comforting language and selective imagery can redirect seekers from inward remembrance toward outer dependency. It is an example of narrative mimicry: light without law, compassion without comprehension. Source reference: https://www.gaia.com/article/who-are-the-pleiadians
docs.title: Origin And Suppression Of Cosmic Memory In Human Lineage

docs.creator: Harrington, Joel F. (Joel Francis)
description: "The extraordinary story of a Renaissance-era executioner and his world, based on a rare and overlooked journal In the late 1500s a Nuremberg man named Frantz Schmidt began to do something utterly remarkable for his era: he started keeping a journal. But what makes Schmidt even more compelling to us is his day job. For forty-five years, Schmidt was an efficient and prolific public executioner, employed by the state to extract confessions and put convicted criminals to death. In his years of service, he executed 361 people and tortured, flogged, or disfigured hundreds more. Is it possible that a man who practiced such cruelty could also be insightful, compassionate, humane--even progressive? In his groundbreaking book, the historian Joel F. Harrington looks for the answer in Schmidt's journal, whose immense significance has been ignored until now. Harrington uncovers details of Schmidt's medical practice, his marriage to a woman ten years older than him, his efforts at penal reform, his almost touching obsession with social status, and most of all his conflicted relationship with his own craft and the growing sense that it could not be squared with his faith. A biography of an ordinary man struggling for his soul, The Faithful Executioner is also an unparalleled portrait of Europe on the cusp of modernity, yet riven by conflict and encumbered by paranoia, superstition, and abuses of power. In his intimate portrait of a Nuremberg executioner, Harrington also sheds light on our own fraught historical moment"--

"A work of nonfiction that explores the thoughts and experiences of one early modern executioner, Nuremberg's Frantz Schmidt (1555-1634), through his own words - a rare personal journal, in which he recorded and described all the executions and corporal punishments he administered between 1573 and his retirement in 1617"--
docs.title: The faithful executioner : life and death, honor and shame in the turbulent Sixteenth Century
